questions.stem: A client presents 90 minutes after sudden focal neurologic deficits and is being considered for reperfusion therapy. Why is urgent brain imaging obtained before treatment?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Brain imaging is obtained mainly to determine the client's blood type before reperfusion, because transfusion compatibility determines eligibility for thrombolysis.","B":"Brain imaging is obtained mainly to confirm that every ischemic stroke is already visible, because absence of an infarct on early imaging excludes acute stroke.","C":"Brain imaging is essential to exclude intracranial hemorrhage before reperfusion therapy, because hemorrhage would change management and make thrombolysis unsafe.","D":"Brain imaging is used mainly to identify chronic neurologic disease before treatment, because excluding acute hemorrhage is not necessary when onset is witnessed."}}
questions.rationale: The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline states that brain imaging is essential before reperfusion therapy to exclude intracranial hemorrhage; noncontrast CT can rapidly detect acute bleeding. Option C states that purpose. Option A incorrectly makes blood typing the reason for brain imaging. Option B incorrectly requires a visible early infarct to confirm ischemic stroke. Option D incorrectly says acute hemorrhage need not be excluded when the onset time is known.
questions.source_name: AHA/ASA — 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
questions.source_detail: Section 3.2 states that brain imaging is essential to exclude hemorrhage in patients eligible for acute ischemic-stroke reperfusion therapy and that noncontrast CT rapidly detects acute intracranial hemorrhage; currentness was rechecked after the July 2026 guideline correction.

qc.qc_note: Strict final audit: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; keyed option within 10% of distractor mean; keyed option is neither shortest nor longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility, grammatical parallelism, and answer-cue leakage.
